info.description: GET only. clearance-api reads what the Clearance core committed. Writes go to the core (POST /v1/clearances/{id}/clear and /deny, /v1/provenance, /v1/records); the runtime's reads and writes (sessions, tasks, agents and their holds, the human inbox, events, results, runtimes) are the AI gateway's. Generated by tools/contract -api from the route table and the Go types (internal/api); do not edit.
info.title: clearance-api

get.summary: The non-secret attestation configuration a portal needs: whether this api can verify (verifiable), the backends, Rekor's public URL and the link to an entry, the keyless identity and issuer, the static key ids and the offline verify command. Public keys only

The signed change attestations, newest first (the cursor is record_seq, the deploy.attestation record's seq): each with its change (app, env, release, tree digest), when it was signed, the envelope digest, backend, key id, Rekor log index and uuid, the deploy.outcome it attests and this replica's last verification. since and until bound the time signed. A person sees the attestations of the changes they may see. For the changes applied and not yet attested, GET /v1/clearances/counts?by=attestation (pending)

The deployment gate's baseline policy: the tier table, the people each tier needs, the outside groups, the TTL, the outage policy by tier (allow-and-record or hold). A repo's clearance.yaml can only tighten it

The deployment gate's changes, newest first: tier and why, state (holding, cleared, denied, expired, superseded, degraded, exception), the requirement and the approvals so far, what the grant binds to. A person sees their apps' changes and the ones their groups may clear; the cursor is updated_at. cluster=<c>&state=cleared is the grant feed: the cluster's cleared changes whose clearance token is live, each with its token; a feed reader (CLEARANCE_API_FEED_READERS) may read only that, for its own clusters

Changes counted by state, tier, app, env, cleared_by or attestation (the C1 stats: holding, cleared by policy and by people, denied). by=attestation: attested (a signed attestation is stored), pending (the deploy reported an applied outcome and none is stored yet: the signer is waiting or retrying) and none (no applied outcome)
One change: the objects and paths it touches, every reason for its tier, the requirement, the approvals, the checks as last reported, and its live clearance token (null when it has none)

The change's signed attestation (C-2) as a Sigstore bundle: the DSSE envelope of an in-toto statement (predicate https://clearance.hangarplatform.dev/change-attestation/v1) and the certificate and Rekor entry that verify it. `clearance attest verify` checks it offline. 404 until a deploy reports an applied outcome

The stored attestation verified server-side exactly as `clearance attest verify` does: its signature against the configured trust (a static key, or a keyless trust root with the core's identity and issuer), the Rekor entry, and that the statement names the change's cleared digest (tree, or terraform plan) and this change. {verified, checked_at, subject, key_id, rekor{log_index, integrated_time, verified}, errors}. Answers 200 with verified false and the reasons for a bundle that fails; 404 when the change has no attestation or this deployment has no trust configured. The answer is remembered per attestation digest until the replica restarts (`cached`); the lists show it as `verification`

One change's history: its deploy.* records (request, clear, answer, outcome, attestation, exception, ...) in chain order, each with its seq, hash, tool, ts, principal and the record. The cursor is seq. Seen by whoever may see the change; secret-bearing keys in a record's state_change are redacted for all but an auditor
This contract

With no scope, the statements of every scope observed in the window ({from, to, scopes: [statement...], truncated}; at most 100 scopes). With no scope and names=only, just the scope list ({from, to, scopes: [{scope}...], truncated, names_only: true}; at most 1000 names, no statements built: one cheap read); names is only, and takes no scope (400). The coverage statement for a scope and window (from and to, RFC 3339; default the last 24 hours): what was cleared and verified, what was seen and not cleared (by coverage state, with how each ended), what could not be seen (the stretches a feed was blind or degraded, and the audit gaps), and the health of each feed, with each item's newest resolution (state, cause, who set it and when) and how many of the window's observations had their source verified (source_integrity). clean is true only when nothing was seen uncleared and every feed was healthy for the whole window: a window with no healthy health record, or whose last record has gone stale, is blind and never clean. Any signed-in person, a delegate for one, an auditor or a configured observation reader (O-5): the whole scope; secret-bearing keys in a record's state_change are redacted for all but an auditor
The agent definitions Clearance decides with: the bundled set and the cluster pins the core stored, each with its source; rejected pins with the reason. full=1 (auditors) adds instructions

Evidence records you may see, newest first; the cursor is seq. outcomes=include (default), exclude or only: the outcome records the core writes beside each allowed decision (outcome_of). installation=<id> keeps one GitHub App installation's records (principal app:<id>). coverage=<state>[,<state>...] keeps the records in those coverage states (authorized-and-verified, observed-not-attributed, out-of-band-detected, coverage-unavailable, break-glass, attempted-refused)

Records you may see, counted by rule, tool, agent, app, decision, coverage, provider (the registered provider or gate that wrote it) or boundary (`by`), with the same filters as the list, and scope=<scope> for one observed scope's records. bucket=1m|5m|15m|1h|6h|1d cuts the window (since is required, until defaults to now, at most 1500 buckets) into epoch-aligned time buckets: each item is then a bucket (its start) and a key, in time order, at most 10000. outcomes=exclude (default) counts each decision once; include or only count the outcome records too. by=cost sums what runs cost instead, per task (default: the task tree), session (one run), agent or principal (`per`): the model-call outcomes' usage (charged_tokens is what the model proxy charged the session budgets) and the run.finish records' runs and wall seconds; each item's count is its model calls
The whole chain checked from genesis: ok, count, head, the first bad seq
One evidence record with its hash

The packet's exceptions, newest first; the cursor is seq: every deploy.exception (kind=out-of-band, drift, untraced-apply, digest-mismatch, attempted-refused or monitoring-protection), every provider's degraded-mode report (deploy.degraded: what it did while the core was unreachable, with the outage policy it was held to), every break-glass window (breakglass.open, breakglass.close with what changed in it) and every runtime read allowed during an outage (tool.call, coverage-unavailable). tool narrows to one of those. Any signed-in person, a delegate for one, an auditor or a configured observation reader reads every exception (O-5); secret-bearing keys in a record's state_change and exception are redacted for all but an auditor

The Clearance GitHub App's installations as the records name them (app:<id>): the account and last action of the last app.installation record, the status it leaves, the records by tool, their seq and ts bounds, and the repositories its checks ran on

The cluster's signed grant feed: a DSSE envelope (application/vnd.clearance.grant-feed.v1+json, the token key) over every clearance token live on the cluster when the core signed it, with seq, iat, exp and each token's payload digest, and the tokens it lists beside it. The core re-signs it on every token write and at least every 2 minutes (exp 5 minutes): verify it whole before acting (docs/gate.md). A feed reader reads its own clusters'; auditors any
The clearance token verification keys, a JWKS (EC P-256, ES256, kid = the RFC 7638 thumbprint): the key the core signs with and keys retired within the last 24 hours. Public

The coverage map in one read (from and to, RFC 3339; default the last 24 hours). The declared registry joined with the records, computed in a fixed number of aggregate queries: nodes (gate types with their instances, mode mix and what they decided; target groups and their targets with coverage mix, observer health and lanes; observers), edges (a gate type or observer to a group, or, with expand=<group>[,<group>], to each of its targets: volume is decisions, status the worst state), the needs-attention list (targets with no gate, blind or degraded observers, gates in flag mode, changes holding, declared gates that decided nothing and decisions from gates nobody declared) and `partial`: what the records cannot yet say. target=<id> is the one-target detail (also the changes moving through it, its exceptions and recent evidence); group=<g> narrows to one cluster or account. Observation facts are whole-scope for every reader (O-5); gate decisions, exceptions and evidence are the records the viewer may see

The observation records (clearance.evidence/v1.1) of one scope, newest first; the cursor is seq. kind=observation (default), assessment, resolution (every edit of a resolution is a record of its own: the history) or observation.verification (a feed's later proof an observation was delivered unaltered). scope is required: the account, cluster or workspace observed; source narrows to one feed. Any signed-in person, a delegate for one, an auditor or a configured observation reader (O-5): the whole scope; secret-bearing keys in a record's state_change are redacted for all but an auditor

The health of the feeds behind a scope's observations, newest first: observation.health records (healthy, degraded or blind per source, with the checks that produced it) and the observation.audit-gap records written when a feed dropped. scope is required. Any signed-in person, a delegate for one, an auditor or a configured observation reader (O-5): the whole scope; secret-bearing keys in a record's state_change are redacted for all but an auditor
The policy in force: the deny rules in evaluation order (id, name, CEL expression, message, hint, bundle, `pack`), the tool registry with tiers, "core" and the loaded bundles (`packs`)
Would this be allowed? A dry run of the real policy for an agent, a tool and its args (JSON) on a fresh session: the decision and each rule's verdict in order. Records nothing
The agent-gate verdicts recorded for a PR (provenance.verify). installation=<id> keeps the verdicts that GitHub App installation recorded
PR receipts: what Clearance's agents opened on a repo (and PR), the commit, the paths. installation=<id> keeps the receipts of pull requests that GitHub App installation checked

get.summary: Server-sent events of new evidence records (event: record, the record as getEvidence serves it) and gate state changes (event: clearance: the deploy.* record's seq, tool and ts and the change summary it recorded), each with id: <seq>. Resume with Last-Event-ID (or after=<seq>); without either the stream starts at the head. types=records,clearances (default both). The same scoping as the reads: a person sees the records and changes they may read; a feed reader only clearance events of its clusters. A comment every 15 s keeps it open; the server ends it after 10 minutes (reconnect with Last-Event-ID)

The declared target registry: what each publishing source (a cluster's gitops render, an account's bootstrap) declares should be protected, the union of every source's set (PUT /v1/targets/{source} on the core). A target has an id, name, kind (k8s-namespace, k8s-cluster, aws-account, github-environment, other), group (the cluster or account), env, app, owner, registry tier (a name), the coverage scope its observations arrive under, its gates (type, instance, mode enforce or flag) and its observers (provider, source); sources lists each set's digest (the one its targets.load record carries). A declaration, not evidence: GET /v1/map reconciles it with the records
